Ben / Marissa —

Attached are the artifacts from the sensitivity sweep we ran this morning. Summary highlights (executive bullets):
- Latency-concurrency behavior: under the baseline config (batching=auto, kv cache enabled, q8) median latency degrades linearly after concurrency ~40 for short prompts, ~24 for medium, and ~8 for long prompts; P95 shows earlier degradation (approx 0.6x of those concntrys).
- Batching impact: increasing batch window to 25ms reduced median per-token CPU by ~12% at high-concurrency workloads but added ~10-18ms to median latency for short prompts. For medium/long prompts batching gives net cost wins with modest latency impact.
- KV cache sizing: smaller per-replica KV caches produced higher tail variance under multi-tenant synthetic mixes; recommend conservative cache allocation for customer SLAs.
- Quantization: q4 reduces GPU memory and improves overall throughput by 20-28% on long sequences but increases median token-latency by ~6-9ms because decode kernels are different; tradeoff depends on whether price-per-token or latency is primary.

We included: omni_perf_snapshot_q3_2028.xlsx (summary sheets + charts), sensitivity-run-summary-2028-09-14.pdf (narrative + methodology), and test-harness-config.yml (exact harness with endpoint flags, traffic mix generator seeds, and autoscaler rules).

Methodology notes (short): all runs executed against a dedicated single-region cluster using redwood-econ-13B-q8 and redwood-econ-13B-q4 variants. Concurrency sweep: linear ramp from 1 to 512 concurrent clients per endpoint, 5 minute steady-state at each step, 3 independent trials per point. Sampled both median and P95/P99 latencies, and collected per-token GPU-time and batch sizes. Load generator used provided OmniRetail prompt distribution when available; otherwise used our commercial baseline.

Caveats: these are representative lab runs; network jitter and multi-region routing in customer envs will alter absolute numbers. We call out relative deltas and sensitivity rather than raw single-number guarantees.

If you want a short meeting to walk through the charts with Laura and procurement, I can run through the workbook.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Laura —

Thanks for the prompt. Attached are the deliverables we promised: a one-page synthesis (first tab in the workbook), a short appendix with methodology and run notes (PDF), and the exact harness config (YAML). Executive summary in one paragraph: under our hosted baseline, latency sensitivity is dominated by prompt length and concurrency; batching and quantization materially change unit economics but with known latency tradeoffs (see bullets). We recommend:
1) If OmniRetail prioritizes 95th-percentile latency for chat experiences, keep q8 and prioritize larger KV caches + conservative batching windows.
2) If throughput/cost dominates for long completions (batch-reporting jobs), consider q4 with larger batch windows.
